value.x-reason: basis unknown requires value: null; unknown is never quietly turned into a guess
a fact with a known basis needs a value; say basis: unknown when the value is missing

basis_rule.description: basis unknown requires value null; any other basis requires a value.

code_ref.description: A source file (and optionally a line range and its copied text). root application: path is inside the application's local copy; root records: path is inside the records folder.

then.x-reason: a count with a known basis needs a value or a formula

count.description: A count with its scope and basis. It carries a value, or a formula over input properties, or (basis unknown) neither.

x-required-reasons.scope: every count needs a scope (per_sweep, per_call, per_run, per_trial); an unscoped count must not be multiplied or compared

evidence_refs.description: IDs of this record's provenance entries that support the fact.

extensa_campaign_id.description: The one Extensa campaign-ID pattern (2026-10-05 ET): record tags, review origins, campaign files (`swdb.campaign`) and the child-process tag (`swdb.workflow`) all use it.
extensa_campaign_id.x-reason: campaign must be an Extensa campaign ID extensa-(native|gem5)-bfs-YYYYMMDD-<letter><n>

fact.description: A fact with its basis. basis unknown requires value null; any other basis requires a value.

x-required-reasons.basis: every fact states its basis (measured, simulated, code_reading, reported, inferred, estimated, unknown)

provider_pin.description: Probata ticket 12 (2026-10-14 ET): the provider kind, model and effort pinned in the run plan (map decision 23 items 5, 7), for example {kind: codex, model: gpt-5.6-sol, effort: xhigh}. One rule for proposals and proof records (S10).

kind.x-reason: a provider kind is codex or claude (swdb.provider_adapters.PINS)

x-required-reasons.effort: a provider pin names its effort
x-required-reasons.kind: a provider pin names the provider kind
x-required-reasons.model: a provider pin names its model

run_index.description: Probata ticket 12 (2026-10-14 ET): which of the three independent runs of a configuration with an LLM this record belongs to. Absent: not part of a repeated run. One rule for proposals and proof records (S10).
run_index.x-reason: run_index is 1, 2 or 3 (three independent runs of an LLM configuration; map decision 23 item 5)

deprecated_by.x-reason: a deprecated record must name its replacement in deprecated_by

then.x-reason: a deprecated record must name its replacement in deprecated_by

x-required-reasons.campaign: an Extensa-mode record names its campaign

x-required-reasons.mode: an Extensa campaign tag is allowed only on mode: extensa records

envelope.description: Merged into every kind schema by swdb. `x-vocab` names a file in vocab/; `x-ref` names the record kind an ID must resolve to; `x-reason` is the message shown when the rule fails. Kind schemas may use the shared `$defs` below as `#/$defs/<name>`.

campaign.description: Extensa campaign ID tag set when the record is created; absent means ArchEvolve mode.

mode.description: Extensa-mode tag set when the record is created (2026-10-03 ET); absent means ArchEvolve mode.
mode.x-reason: mode is extensa or absent (ArchEvolve mode)

envelope.title: Envelope: the fields every record starts with

x-required-reasons.assumptions: a proof record that is not a skip states its assumption set (an empty list when none)
x-required-reasons.bounds: a proof record that is not a skip states its bounds
x-required-reasons.evidence: a proof record that is not a skip names its adapter log
x-required-reasons.verdict: a proof record that is not a skip states its verdict

assumptions.x-reason: a skip record carries no assumption set (no verifier ran)

bounds.x-reason: a skip record carries no bounds (no verifier ran)

evidence.x-reason: a skip record names no adapter log (no verifier ran)

verdict.x-reason: a skip record carries no verdict (no verifier ran)

unreplayed_counterexample.x-reason: only a not-proven record holds an unreplayed counterexample
only a record of failure class spurious_counterexample holds an unreplayed counterexample

x-required-reasons.unreplayed_counterexample: a spurious_counterexample record holds the counterexample that did not replay

counterexample.x-reason: only a refuted record holds a counterexample

replay_label.x-reason: only a refuted record holds a replay label

x-required-reasons.counterexample: a refuted record holds its counterexample inline

failure_class.x-reason: only a not-proven record names a failure class

x-required-reasons.failure_class: a not-proven record names its failure class

kind.x-reason: only a candidate proof unit carries a proof route

additionalProperties.x-reason: a bounded_direct record is capped at proven within bounds (ticket 61; map 24 item 1): no dimension is unbounded

threads.x-reason: a bounded_direct record is capped at proven within bounds, threads = 1 (ticket 61; map 24 item 1): its thread count is 1

proof.description: One record per proof job, written by `swdb prove` into records/proofs/ and never edited. A candidate artifact's level is computed on read from the proof records whose pins still match (swdb.proof). Documented in docs/reference/format-v0.4-proof.md.

assumptions.description: The assumption set. Each entry: kind (one of seven), reference (ID and hash), one plain sentence.

sentence.x-reason: an assumption sentence is not empty

x-required-reasons.sentence: every assumption entry states itself in one plain sentence

additionalProperties.x-reason: a bound is a positive integer or "unbounded"

bounds.description: One value or "unbounded" per bound dimension; the thread count is always present.

x-required-reasons.threads: every proof record bounds the thread count (a value or "unbounded")

counterexample.description: A refuted verdict's counterexample, inline (small; needed for replay and repair).

adapter_log.description: The adapter's log in a runs folder outside the repo, on the host the job ran on.

reports.description: Ticket 21: the verifier's own reports and inputs in the runs folder (WP input, WP log, per-goal and per-property reports, the handler's output), each by name, absolute path and sha256.

evidence_kind.x-reason: evidence_kind is contract_fixture (scripted adapter, or a contract_fixture method version) or execution (a real verifier under a real method version; ticket 21)

failure_class.description: Why a not-proven verdict was not proven: a value of vocabulary proof_failure_classes whose role is failure_class (ticket 11; the role is checked in swdb.proof.validate_record).

goals.description: Ticket 36: every generated goal, with source wp_json or wp_inventory and a smoke marker. Automatic goals and successful smoke tests may have no proving solver/time; smoke passed means the false reachability goal was not proven.

hint_check.description: Ticket 35: the proof hint check's result (check and vocabulary versions, verdict, every rejection by rule); a rejected set never reaches WP.

reached_wp.x-reason: a rejected hint set never reaches WP

rejections.x-reason: a rejected hint set names each rejection
an accepted hint set has no rejection

hint_set.description: Ticket 35: the hint set the job was given (records in the given order) and its hash (anchor, kind and text of each record, in canonical order).

seed_source.x-reason: only a seed names a seed source

x-required-reasons.seed_source: a seed names where it came from

x-required-reasons.provenance: every hint says who wrote it: agent, seed (with its source) or human (map 13 item 9)

job.description: The job block (ticket 12 owns this one field list and its checks; 04 writes it, 57 fills it on mbit10, and neither adds a field). Proof time is a cost metric, never a speed claim.

adapter.description: The verifier adapter's name (`scripted` for contract fixtures).

batch.description: Batch ID; the jobs of one `swdb prove` call share it.

batch_load.description: The host's 1-minute load average {start, end}, sampled when the job starts and ends. A bare number: written before ticket 12 (start only).
batch_load.x-reason: batch_load is {start, end}, each a load average of at least 0 (a bare number: written before ticket 12)

cpu_seconds.description: CPU time of the job (own process and waited children).

host.description: The run host: `mac` on the Mac, the host's short name elsewhere (mbit10).

peak_rss_bytes.description: Largest resident set size of the job's whole process tree: what the 8 GB RSS watchdog per worker reads (O9).

position.description: Position in the batch (57 checks interleaving from batch and position).

worker_core.description: The one core the job was pinned to, or "unpinned" (macOS pins nothing). null: written before ticket 12 (04's form for unpinned).
worker_core.x-reason: worker_core is a core number, "unpinned", or null (written before ticket 12)

x-required-reasons.adapter: the job block names the verifier adapter, so a scripted record shows as such
x-required-reasons.batch: the job block names its batch
x-required-reasons.batch_load: the job block holds the host's batch load
x-required-reasons.cpu_seconds: the job block holds the job's CPU time
x-required-reasons.host: the job block names the host (mac on the Mac), so Mac and mbit10 numbers never mix
x-required-reasons.peak_rss_bytes: the job block holds the job's peak RSS (what the 8 GB RSS watchdog reads, O9)
x-required-reasons.position: the job block holds its position in the batch
x-required-reasons.wall_seconds: the job block holds the job's wall time
x-required-reasons.worker_core: the job block names the worker core ("unpinned" when the host pins none)

level.x-reason: a proof record never holds a level: the level rule computes it on read (ADR 0016)

level_rule.x-reason: a proof record never pins the level rule (26 item 9): a rule change recomputes levels and voids no proof

method_part_status.description: Ticket 42: a checked theorem or its written fallback, separate from record lifecycle status.

pins.description: The content-hash set: one pin per kind. A pin that does not apply yet is written as {not_applicable: <sentence>}, never left out.

baseline_c_lowering.description: Ticket 61: whole-function equivalence: the baseline function's C lowering in the product program, {id: <function>.c, sha256 of its text}. Optional: only whole-function jobs write it.

c_lowering.description: Ticket 21: the C lowering the verifier ran on, {id: <function>.c, sha256 of its text}. Optional: only adapters that run on a C lowering write it.

heap_model_foundations.description: Selected Why3 and Frama-C standard arithmetic/map/datatype support sources.

heap_model_view_check.description: Exact original-model source to unbounded heap VC translation and prelaunch checker.

helper_window_certificate.description: Checked source/view argument captures, call order and dependency certificate.

helper_window_check.description: Checker for the exact contextual helper source transformation.

logic.description: Ticket 26: every logic-library file the proof used (the formal halves' acsl.uses, or the file a prove-logic job checked), each by ID, version and file sha256. Optional: written only when a file is used. The level rule stops counting the record when a file's sha256 changes.

models.description: Ticket 24: the C models the C lowering calls (std::min, __atomic_*, ...), each by name, sha256 of its text and its proven c_model proof record (`swdb prove --model NAME`). Optional: written by the wp adapter when the unit's lowering calls a model.

naming_rules.description: Ticket 24: the C lowering's naming rules, {id: kept-names.<n>, sha256 of the rules text} (swdb.c_lowering.naming_rules()). Written with c_lowering; a new rules version gives a different pin.

standard_model_view_certificate.description: Original/view contract, C-AST guard and exact text mapping certificate.

standard_model_view_check.description: The checked pure defensive-at guard to named proof obligation relation.

standard_range_call_check.description: Original-source typed std::copy roots, endpoint offsets, capacity and qualified model dependency checker.

standard_range_model_certificate.description: Explicit typed iterator-range qualification, unchanged contract and checked numerical obligations.

standard_range_model_check.description: Checker for exact range-qualified standard model source/view semantics.

std_models.description: Ticket 25: the std::vector and std::pair model version the C lowering used, {id: swdb-std-models-<version>, sha256 of swdb/std_models.py} (swdb.std_models.identity()). Written exactly when the proof unit uses a modeled type; changing any member's contract gives a different pin.

assumes.description: Ticket 23: the names of the assume statements the summary's generated stub emitted (one per ensures clause), each tagged in the stub with the entry and its sha256.

terminal_release_certificate.description: Hash of the generator-owned AST ownership certificate for one nonescaping scalar-array owner and terminal delete[].

terminal_release_check.description: The ownership checker used to omit a proven-unobservable final delete[] in the WP view; original C lowering and code remain pinned.

translator.description: Ticket 22: the formal-half translator the verifier's input came from, {id: <tool>-<version>, sha256 of the translator's source} (the CBMC translator). Optional: only adapters with a translator write it.

vector_ownership_allocator.description: The explicit fresh-allocation/private-region premise used only by the checked WP view.

vector_ownership_certificate.description: The generated original/view contract, source frame and alias-liveness certificate.

vector_ownership_check.description: The checked scalar-vector relational lowering and source-frame projection.

vector_pipeline_allocator.description: Explicit successful fresh-allocation and preexisting-memory frame premise for the private pipeline.

vector_pipeline_check.description: Exact private vector copy/scan source relation and independently checked C view.

vector_reallocation_model.description: Explicit qualified v3 vector reallocation contract/domain candidate. Separate from the unchanged original std_models catalog; caller discharge and body proof remain mandatory.

x-required-reasons.build_constants: the content-hash set lists every build constant (an empty list when none)

x-required-reasons.contract: the content-hash set pins the contract

x-required-reasons.reference_semantics: the content-hash set pins the reference semantics (or says not_applicable)
x-required-reasons.summaries: the content-hash set lists every summary used (an empty list when none)

proof_setup_check.description: Ticket36 versioned prelaunch check, frozen method and input hashes.

replay_label.description: Refuted only, optional (ticket 10 defines it; ticket 60 fills it and makes it required on refuted records): how far the refutation's strict-layer replay reaches. undefined_behavior is O6's "undefined behavior (no strict-layer replay)": the refutation counts and the batch goes on.
replay_label.x-reason: replay_label is reproduced, proof_semantics_only, not_reproduced or undefined_behavior (O6); ticket 10 owns this field and adds any new value

route.description: Optional proof route of a candidate proof unit (map spec, "Proof routes"). 61 fills bounded_direct; 62 fills route_1 and route_3 and makes it required.
route.x-reason: route is route_1 (direct), route_3 (lockstep) or bounded_direct; ticket 04 owns this field and adds any new value

settings.description: Ticket 21: the frozen settings the verifier ran with (flags, fresh session, default warning levels, machdep, time per solver, environment variables removed, RSS cap, hint count, build constants).

skip_reason.description: A skip: no verifier ran, for this reason (a value of vocabulary proof_failure_classes whose role is skip_reason; ticket 11). A skip record has no verdict, bounds, assumptions or adapter log; the level rule ignores it.

candidate.x-reason: only a candidate proof unit names a candidate artifact

function.x-reason: only a candidate proof unit names a function

x-required-reasons.id: a subject that is not a candidate proof unit names what was proven in `id`

x-required-reasons.candidate: a candidate proof unit names its candidate artifact
x-required-reasons.function: a candidate proof unit names the function that holds the rewrite site

subject.description: What was proven. Only candidate_proof_unit is exercised by ticket 04; the other kinds take a text `id` (and an optional `part`) until the tickets that write them give them a shape.

function.description: The function that holds the rewrite site; one call of it is the proof unit.

part.description: A contract-proof part or method part (vocabulary proof_part_names; its subject_kind must match, checked in swdb.proof.validate_record). Ticket 10.

tools.description: Ticket 10 (S14): the verifiers and solvers the job used, each by the reference ID of a trusted_tool entry in the assumption set (for example frama-c-wp-33.0, z3-4.8.14). swdb validate refuses a tool with no such entry. Optional until the real adapters (21, 22) write it.

unproven_properties.description: Ticket 21: not proven only: each property of the per-property report that is not Valid (the hint loop's input, ticket 37).

unreplayed_counterexample.description: Not proven only (ticket 11, from ticket 05's SAW spike): a counterexample the verifier reported that did not replay concretely on the compiled code, so it is a tool or encoding failure, never a refutation, and never reaches repair. Required exactly when failure_class is spurious_counterexample (Yan-Ru 2026-10-14 02:25 ET).

verdict_reading.description: Ticket36 fresh-run reader version and outcome.

proof.title: Proof record: one proof job, never changed (ADR 0016; Probata proof of concept ticket 04, 2026-10-14 ET)
